title: HYPERPARAMETER HUNT
subtitle: Find the best settings — but every experiment costs GPU time.

intro.headline: You have 25 GPU hours
intro.body: Each tile is one training run. Click to spend an hour and see the validation accuracy. Somewhere in here is the best combination — but you cannot afford to try them all, and the tile you spend now is a tile you cannot spend later.

strategies.bayesianLike: Concentrating near your best result — that is exploitation.
strategies.randomSearch: Spreading out across the space — that is exploration.

foundGlobal.title: Found the optimum
foundGlobal.body: You reached {bestValue}% at ({bestX}, {bestY}) using {reveals} of {budget} experiments, spending {exploitPercent}% of them near your best-known point. That is Bayesian optimization done by hand: sample a little, then let the good results pull your next sample toward them. Real tuners do exactly this, they just keep a probabilistic model of the surface instead of a hunch.

foundLocal.title: Stuck on a local optimum
foundLocal.body: You topped out at {bestValue}%, but {globalValue}% was sitting somewhere you never looked. You committed to the first promising region — {exploitPercent}% of your experiments clustered near your running best. That is the exploitation trap: every experiment spent confirming a good result is one not spent finding a better one, and the surface never tells you which peak you are standing on.

scattered.title: Explorer at heart
scattered.body: You found {bestValue}% by covering {uniqueRegions} separate regions in {reveals} experiments. Pure exploration does find the global optimum — it just pays full price for it. A tuner that started narrowing after the first few hits would have got here in roughly {optimalReveals}. Exploration buys information; exploitation spends it.

titleScreen.flavor: The best settings are hiding. Compute is finite.
titleScreen.instructions: Click a tile to run that experiment. Green is good. You get 25.
